question.text: The standard reaction Gibbs energy for a chemical reaction at an absolute temperature $\mathrm{T}$ is given by $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}=\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{BT}$ where A and $B$ are non-zero constants. Which of the following is true about this reaction?

solution.text:
$\Delta G^{\circ}=A-B T$

A and B are non-zero constants

$\therefore \Delta G^{\circ}=\Delta H^{\circ}-T \Delta S^{\circ}=A-B T$

$\therefore$ Reaction will be endothermic if $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}>0 .$

Hence, $\mathrm{A}>0$ and $\mathrm{B}  < 0$
